verses.original: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες ἀκούσατέ μου τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς νυνὶ ἀπολογίας
verses.transliteration: Andres adelphoi kai pateres akousate mou tēs pros hymas nyni apologias
verses.literal: Brothers and fathers listen now to my defense before you
verses.literalPt: HOMENS, irmãos e pais, ouvi agora a minha defesa perante vós

verses.original: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ὅτι τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ προσεφώνει αὐτοῖς μᾶλλον παρέσχον ἡσυχίαν Καὶ φησίν
verses.transliteration: akousantes de hoti tē Hebraidi dialektō prosephōnei autois mallon pareschon hēsychian Kai phēsin
verses.literal: When they heard him speak to them in Hebrew . . . they became even more quiet Then Paul declared
verses.literalPt: (E, quando ouviram falar-lhes em língua hebraica, maior silêncio guardaram). E disse:

verses.original: Ἐγώ εἰμι ἀνὴρ Ἰουδαῖος γεγεννημένος ἐν Ταρσῷ τῆς Κιλικίας ἀνατεθραμμένος δὲ ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ παρὰ τοὺς πόδας Γαμαλιήλ πεπαιδευμένος κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν τοῦ πατρῴου νόμου ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τοῦ Θεοῦ καθὼς πάντες ὑμεῖς ἐστε σήμερον
verses.transliteration: Egō eimi anēr Ioudaios gegennēmenos en Tarsō tēs Kilikias anatethrammenos de en tē polei tautē para tous podas Gamaliēl pepaideumenos kata akribeian tou patrōou nomou zēlōtēs hyparchōn tou Theou kathōs pantes hymeis este sēmeron
verses.literal: I am a Jew . . . born in Tarsus of Cilicia but raised in this city I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers I was just as zealous for God as any of you are today
verses.literalPt: Quanto a mim, sou judeu, nascido em Tarso da Cilícia, e nesta cidade criado aos pés de Gamaliel, instruído conforme a verdade da lei de nossos pais, zeloso de Deus, como todos vós hoje sois.

verses.original: ὃς ταύτην τὴν Ὁδὸν ἐδίωξα ἄχρι θανάτου δεσμεύων καὶ παραδιδοὺς εἰς φυλακὰς ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας
verses.transliteration: hos tautēn tēn Hodon ediōxa achri thanatou desmeuōn kai paradidous eis phylakas andras te kai gynaikas
verses.literal: I persecuted this Way even to the death detaining both men and women and throwing them into prison
verses.literalPt: E persegui este caminho até à morte, prendendo, e pondo em prisões, tanto homens como mulheres,

verses.original: ὡς καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς μαρτυρεῖ μοι καὶ πᾶν τὸ πρεσβυτέριον παρ’ ὧν καὶ ἐπιστολὰς δεξάμενος πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς εἰς Δαμασκὸν ἐπορευόμην ἄξων καὶ τοὺς ἐκεῖσε ὄντας δεδεμένους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἵνα τιμωρηθῶσιν
verses.transliteration: hōs kai ho archiereus martyrei moi kai pan to presbyterion par’ hōn kai epistolas dexamenos pros tous adelphous eis Damaskon eporeuomēn axōn kai tous ekeise ontas dedemenous eis Ierousalēm hina timōrēthōsin
verses.literal: as the high priest and the whole Council can testify about me I even obtained letters from them to their brothers in Damascus and I was on my way to apprehend these people . . . . . . and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished
verses.literalPt: Como também o sumo sacerdote me é testemunha, e todo o conselho dos anciãos. E, recebendo destes cartas para os irmãos, fui a Damasco, para trazer maniatados para Jerusalém aqueles que ali estivessem, a fim de que fossem castigados.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι πορευομένῳ καὶ ἐγγίζοντι τῇ Δαμασκῷ περὶ μεσημβρίαν ἐξαίφνης ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ περιαστράψαι φῶς ἱκανὸν περὶ ἐμέ
verses.transliteration: Egeneto de moi poreuomenō kai engizonti tē Damaskō peri mesēmbrian exaiphnēs ek tou ouranou periastrapsai phōs hikanon peri eme
verses.literal: About noon as I was approaching Damascus suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me
verses.literalPt: Ora, aconteceu que, indo eu já de caminho, e chegando perto de Damasco, quase ao meio-dia, de repente me rodeou uma grande luz do céu.

verses.original: ἔπεσά τε εἰς τὸ ἔδαφος καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι Σαοὺλ Σαούλ τί με διώκεις
verses.transliteration: epesa te eis to edaphos kai ēkousa phōnēs legousēs moi Saoul Saoul ti me diōkeis
verses.literal: I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me Saul Saul why do you persecute Me
verses.literalPt: E caí por terra, e ouvi uma voz que me dizia: Saulo, Saulo, por que me persegues?

verses.original: Ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπεκρίθην Τίς εἶ Κύριε Εἶπέν τε πρὸς ἐμέ Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὃν σὺ διώκεις
verses.transliteration: Egō de apekrithēn Tis ei Kyrie Eipen te pros eme Egō eimi Iēsous ho Nazōraios hon sy diōkeis
verses.literal: Who are You Lord I asked I am Jesus of Nazareth whom you are persecuting He replied
verses.literalPt: E eu respondi: Quem és, Senhor? E disse-me: Eu sou Jesus Nazareno, a quem tu persegues.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ ὄντες τὸ μὲν φῶς ἐθεάσαντο τὴν δὲ φωνὴν οὐκ ἤκουσαν τοῦ λαλοῦντός μοι
verses.transliteration: hoi de syn emoi ontes to men phōs etheasanto tēn de phōnēn ouk ēkousan tou lalountos moi
verses.literal: My companions . . . . . . . . . saw the light but they could not understand the voice of the One speaking to me
verses.literalPt: E os que estavam comigo viram, em verdade, a luz, e se atemorizaram muito, mas não ouviram a voz daquele que falava comigo.

verses.original: Εἶπον δέ Τί ποιήσω Κύριε Ὁ δὲ Κύριος εἶπεν πρός με Ἀναστὰς πορεύου εἰς Δαμασκόν κἀκεῖ σοι λαληθήσεται περὶ πάντων ὧν τέτακταί σοι ποιῆσαι
verses.transliteration: Eipon de Ti poiēsō Kyrie Ho de Kyrios eipen pros me Anastas poreuou eis Damaskon kakei soi lalēthēsetai peri pantōn hōn tetaktai soi poiēsai
verses.literal: Then I asked What should I do Lord Get up and go into Damascus - He told . . . me There you will be told all that you have been appointed to do
verses.literalPt: Então disse eu: Senhor, que farei? E o Senhor disse-me: Levanta-te, e vai a Damasco, e ali se te dirá tudo o que te é ordenado fazer.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ οὐκ ἐνέβλεπον ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τοῦ φωτὸς ἐκείνου χειραγωγούμενος ὑπὸ τῶν συνόντων μοι ἦλθον εἰς Δαμασκόν
verses.transliteration: Hōs de ouk eneblepon apo tēs doxēs tou phōtos ekeinou cheiragōgoumenos hypo tōn synontōn moi ēlthon eis Damaskon
verses.literal: Because the brilliance of the light had blinded me - my companions . . . . . . led me by the hand into Damascus
verses.literalPt: E, como eu não via, por causa do esplendor daquela luz, fui levado pela mão dos que estavam comigo, e cheguei a Damasco.

verses.original: Ἁνανίας δέ τις ἀνὴρ εὐλαβὴς κατὰ τὸν νόμον μαρτυρούμενος ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν κατοικούντων Ἰουδαίων
verses.transliteration: Hananias de tis anēr eulabēs kata ton nomon martyroumenos hypo pantōn tōn katoikountōn Ioudaiōn
verses.literal: There a man named Ananias a devout observer of the law who was highly regarded by all the Jews living there
verses.literalPt: E um certo Ananias, homem piedoso conforme a lei, que tinha bom testemunho de todos os judeus que ali moravam,

verses.original: ἐλθὼν πρὸς ἐμὲ καὶ ἐπιστὰς εἶπέν μοι Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ ἀνάβλεψον κἀγὼ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἀνέβλεψα εἰς αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: elthōn pros eme kai epistas eipen moi Saoul adelphe anablepson kagō autē tē hōra aneblepsa eis auton
verses.literal: came and stood beside me Brother Saul he said receive your sight And at that moment I could see . . . him
verses.literalPt: Vindo ter comigo, e apresentando-se, disse-me: Saulo, irmão, recobra a vista. E naquela mesma hora o vi.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν προεχειρίσατό σε γνῶναι τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰδεῖν τὸν Δίκαιον καὶ ἀκοῦσαι φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen Ho Theos tōn paterōn hēmōn proecheirisato se gnōnai to thelēma autou kai idein ton Dikaion kai akousai phōnēn ek tou stomatos autou
verses.literal: Then he said The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will and to see the Righteous One and to hear His voice . . . . . . . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: E ele disse: O Deus de nossos pais de antemão te designou para que conheças a sua vontade, e vejas aquele Justo e ouças a voz da sua boca.

verses.original: ὅτι ἔσῃ μάρτυς αὐτῷ πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὧν ἑώρακας καὶ ἤκουσας
verses.transliteration: hoti esē martys autō pros pantas anthrōpous hōn heōrakas kai ēkousas
verses.literal: You will be His witness to everyone . . . of what you have seen and heard
verses.literalPt: Porque hás de ser sua testemunha para com todos os homens do que tens visto e ouvido.

verses.original: καὶ νῦν τί μέλλεις ἀναστὰς βάπτισαι καὶ ἀπόλουσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου ἐπικαλεσάμενος τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai nyn ti melleis anastas baptisai kai apolousai tas hamartias sou epikalesamenos to onoma autou
verses.literal: And now what are you waiting for Get up be baptized and wash your sins away calling on His name
verses.literalPt: E agora por que te deténs? Levanta-te, e batiza-te, e lava os teus pecados, invocando o nome do Senhor.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι ὑποστρέψαντι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ προσευχομένου μου ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γενέσθαι με ἐν ἐκστάσει
verses.transliteration: Egeneto de moi hypostrepsanti eis Ierousalēm kai proseuchomenou mou en tō hierō genesthai me en ekstasei
verses.literal: Later when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple I fell into a trance
verses.literalPt: E aconteceu que, tornando eu para Jerusalém, quando orava no templo, fui arrebatado para fora de mim.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν λέγοντά μοι Σπεῦσον καὶ ἔξελθε ἐν τάχει ἐξ Ἰερουσαλήμ διότι οὐ παραδέξονταί σου μαρτυρίαν περὶ ἐμοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai idein auton legonta moi Speuson kai exelthe en tachei ex Ierousalēm dioti ou paradexontai sou martyrian peri emou
verses.literal: and saw the Lord saying to me Hurry Leave . . . Jerusalem quickly because the people here will not accept your testimony about Me
verses.literalPt: E vi aquele que me dizia: Dá-te pressa e sai apressadamente de Jerusalém; porque não receberão o teu testemunho acerca de mim.

verses.original: Κἀγὼ εἶπον Κύριε αὐτοὶ ἐπίστανται ὅτι ἐγὼ ἤμην φυλακίζων καὶ δέρων κατὰ τὰς συναγωγὰς τοὺς πιστεύοντας ἐπὶ σέ
verses.transliteration: Kagō eipon Kyrie autoi epistantai hoti egō ēmēn phylakizōn kai derōn kata tas synagōgas tous pisteuontas epi se
verses.literal: Lord I answered they know very well that in one synagogue after another I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You
verses.literalPt: E eu disse: Senhor, eles bem sabem que eu lançava na prisão e açoitava nas sinagogas os que criam em ti.

verses.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐξεχύννετο τὸ αἷμα Στεφάνου τοῦ μάρτυρός σου καὶ αὐτὸς ἤμην ἐφεστὼς καὶ συνευδοκῶν καὶ φυλάσσων τὰ ἱμάτια τῶν ἀναιρούντων αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: kai hote exechynneto to haima Stephanou tou martyros sou kai autos ēmēn ephestōs kai syneudokōn kai phylassōn ta himatia tōn anairountōn auton
verses.literal: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was shed I stood there giving my approval and watching over the garments of those who killed him
verses.literalPt: E quando o sangue de Estêvão, tua testemunha, se derramava, também eu estava presente, e consentia na sua morte, e guardava as capas dos que o matavam.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν πρός με Πορεύου ὅτι ἐγὼ εἰς ἔθνη μακρὰν ἐξαποστελῶ σε
verses.transliteration: Kai eipen pros me Poreuou hoti egō eis ethnē makran exapostelō se
verses.literal: Then He said to me Go I will send you far away to the Gentiles
verses.literalPt: E disse-me: Vai, porque hei de enviar-te aos gentios de longe.

verses.original: Ἤκουον δὲ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι τούτου τοῦ λόγου καὶ ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν λέγοντες Αἶρε ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς τὸν τοιοῦτον οὐ γὰρ καθῆκεν αὐτὸν ζῆν
verses.transliteration: Ēkouon de autou achri toutou tou logou kai epēran tēn phōnēn autōn legontes Aire apo tēs gēs ton toiouton ou gar kathēken auton zēn
verses.literal: The crowd listened to Paul until he made this statement . . . Then they lifted up their voices and shouted Rid the earth of him He is not fit . . . to live
verses.literalPt: E ouviram-no até esta palavra, e levantaram a voz, dizendo: Tira da terra um tal homem, porque não convém que viva.

verses.original: Κραυγαζόντων τε αὐτῶν καὶ ῥιπτούντων τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ κονιορτὸν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸν ἀέρα
verses.transliteration: Kraugazontōn te autōn kai rhiptountōn ta himatia kai koniorton ballontōn eis ton aera
verses.literal: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air
verses.literalPt: E, clamando eles, e arrojando de si as vestes, e lançando pó para o ar,

verses.original: ἐκέλευσεν ὁ χιλίαρχος εἰσάγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν εἴπας μάστιξιν ἀνετάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιγνῷ δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν οὕτως ἐπεφώνουν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: ekeleusen ho chiliarchos eisagesthai auton eis tēn parembolēn eipas mastixin anetazesthai auton hina epignō di’ hēn aitian houtōs epephōnoun autō
verses.literal: the commander ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks He directed that Paul be flogged and interrogated to determine the reason for this outcry against him
verses.literalPt: O tribuno mandou que o levassem para a fortaleza, dizendo que o examinassem com açoites, para saber por que causa assim clamavam contra ele.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ προέτειναν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἱμᾶσιν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν ἑστῶτα ἑκατόνταρχον ὁ Παῦλος Εἰ ἄνθρωπον Ῥωμαῖον καὶ ἀκατάκριτον ἔξεστιν ὑμῖν μαστίζειν
verses.transliteration: Hōs de proeteinan auton tois himasin eipen pros ton hestōta hekatontarchon ho Paulos Ei anthrōpon Rhōmaion kai akatakriton exestin hymin mastizein
verses.literal: But as they stretched him out . . . to strap him down Paul said to the centurion standing there Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen without a trial
verses.literalPt: E, quando o estavam atando com correias, disse Paulo ao centurião que ali estava: É-vos lícito açoitar um romano, sem ser condenado?

verses.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης προσελθὼν τῷ χιλιάρχῳ ἀπήγγειλεν λέγων Τί μέλλεις ποιεῖν ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Akousas de ho hekatontarchēs proselthōn tō chiliarchō apēngeilen legōn Ti melleis poiein ho gar anthrōpos houtos Rhōmaios estin
verses.literal: On hearing this the centurion went and reported it to the commander What are you going to do he said This man is a Roman citizen
verses.literalPt: E, ouvindo isto, o centurião foi, e anunciou ao tribuno, dizendo: Vê o que vais fazer, porque este homem é romano.

verses.original: Προσελθὼν δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Λέγε μοι σὺ Ῥωμαῖος εἶ Ὁ δὲ ἔφη Ναί
verses.transliteration: Proselthōn de ho chiliarchos eipen autō Lege moi sy Rhōmaios ei Ho de ephē Nai
verses.literal: The commander went to Paul and asked Tell me are you a Roman citizen Yes - he answered
verses.literalPt: E, vindo o tribuno, disse-lhe: Dize-me, és tu romano? E ele disse: Sim.

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος Ἐγὼ πολλοῦ κεφαλαίου τὴν πολιτείαν ταύτην ἐκτησάμην ὁ Δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη Ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ γεγέννημαι
verses.transliteration: Apekrithē de ho chiliarchos Egō pollou kephalaiou tēn politeian tautēn ektēsamēn ho De Paulos ephē Egō de kai gegennēmai
verses.literal: I paid a high price for my citizenship said the commander But I was born a citizen - Paul replied
verses.literalPt: E respondeu o tribuno: Eu com grande soma de dinheiro alcancei este direito de cidadão. Paulo disse: Mas eu o sou de nascimento.

verses.original: Εὐθέως οὖν ἀπέστησαν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ οἱ μέλλοντες αὐτὸν ἀνετάζειν καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος δὲ ἐφοβήθη ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν καὶ ὅτι αὐτὸν ἦν δεδεκώς
verses.transliteration: Eutheōs oun apestēsan ap’ autou hoi mellontes auton anetazein kai ho chiliarchos de ephobēthē epignous hoti Rhōmaios estin kai hoti auton ēn dedekōs
verses.literal: At once . . . those who were about to interrogate Paul stepped back . . . . . . and the commander himself was alarmed when he realized . . . . . . that he had put a Roman citizen in chains
verses.literalPt: E logo dele se apartaram os que o haviam de examinar; e até o tribuno teve temor, quando soube que era romano, visto que o tinha ligado.

verses.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον βουλόμενος γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς τὸ τί κατηγορεῖται ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἔλυσεν αὐτόν καὶ ἐκέλευσεν συνελθεῖν τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ πᾶν τὸ συνέδριον καὶ καταγαγὼν τὸν Παῦλον ἔστησεν εἰς αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: Tē de epaurion boulomenos gnōnai to asphales to ti katēgoreitai hypo tōn Ioudaiōn elysen auton kai ekeleusen synelthein tous archiereis kai pan to synedrion kai katagagōn ton Paulon estēsen eis autous
verses.literal: The next day the commander wanting to learn the real reason . . . Paul was accused by the Jews released him and ordered the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble Then he brought Paul down and had him stand before them
verses.literalPt: E no dia seguinte, querendo saber ao certo a causa por que era acusado pelos judeus, soltou-o das prisões, e mandou vir os principais dos sacerdotes, e todo o seu conselho; e, trazendo Paulo, o apresentou diante deles.
